Wrapped Monero token XMR1 crashes 99% after issuer-linked wallet sells $13.5M –
Link
XMR1, a wrapped Monero token issued by swap service Wagyu and traded on Hyperliquid’s order book, fell from about $488 to $1 in roughly 30 minutes. A wallet funded by the token’s creator address had received 5.2M XMR1 and sold about $13.5M worth. It is still unclear whether the transfers were authorized or the result of compromised credentials. Native Monero and Hyperliquid’s XMR perps were unaffected and kept trading near $482.
Wrapped assets carry the issuer’s risk. When redemption depends on a single bridge operator, one compromised key can wipe out the peg in minutes.

tweet.text:
Can anyone answer: Where is the demand side for Pearl? 

It seems the entire story of Pearl is that it has solved it's supply side. 

Pearl has merged PoW and AI inference, so that these are harmonized, rather than competitive with each-other. Great 👍. That's cool and novel.

They solved the supply side. 

As far as I understand it, Pearl has no answer for the demand side. Demand for Pearl is entirely speculative and reflexive. 

There is simply no reason to hold Pearl as a SoV, or spend Pearl as a commodity. Holding Pearl is simply subsidizing the AI buildout by allowing Pearl miners to sell at a higher price. 

While it's true that this is not fundamentally different than BTC or Gold ('there is no utility or commodity value to BTC"), saying this as a pro-Pearl argument feels incredibly vapid and borderline disingenuous. Just because we have Bitcoin as precedent to point to, doesn't mean that this precedent gets to be applied anywhere else.
